newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee closes flat in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee closes flat in lacklustre trade.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed unchanged against the dollar on Tuesday in lacklustre trading in the absence of commercial demand, dealers said.
The rupee ended at 56.40 for the second day in a row, after opening at the same level and briefly touching 56.45.
"There wasn't much activity except for two buyers -- a state bank and a foreign bank," a Deutsche Bank dealer said. "Overall there was no demand today."
Dealers said the market was inactive in line with overseas lethargy ahead of today's Fed Open Market Committee meeting.
"Our market may be waiting to take a cue from that," a Commercial Bank dealer said.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by a quarter local cent, fixing buying and selling at 55.7519 and 56.8782.

"There is a feeling the rupee has reached a saturation point. If the Central Bank is not overly positive towards the dollar in the coming days, the rupee might even go up," the Commercial Bank dealer said.
Overnight call money closed at 14.5 percent after opening at 14 percent.
